subject: use feature 'extra_paired_delimiters' (5.36) is absent -- PPI 1.291 does not lex the Unicode bracket pairs, so 11 op/lex.t rows fail (4 of them principle-9 invalid-input rows and 3 of them #221)
description:
FILED s473t6b (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 round 9.

PERL 5.36+: `use feature 'extra_paired_delimiters'` (experimental) adds a set
of PAIRED delimiters to the quote-like operators beyond `() [] {} <>` -- the
Unicode bracket pairs, so `qÂ«textÂ»`, `qqãtextã`, `mâ¨patâ©` and their nesting
work, and the closing delimiter must match the opening one.  Outside the
feature's lexical scope the same spellings are ORDINARY characters, so a
program that uses one there is a syntax error -- which is what the test file
asserts in both directions.

PCL: the feature is nowhere in the tree (grepped: no `extra_paired` in
docs/, lib/ or Pl/).  PPI's lexer is asked with PCL's feature state
(`custom_feature_include_cb`, #360), so the delimiters are not recognised and
the in-scope rows fail; the out-of-scope rows, which assert a FAILURE, fail
too (PCL does not validate -- principle 9).

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/lex.t
  37 `Various tests of string delims \xAB/\xBB returned without error`
  38 `And the expected number of warnings were generated`
  39 `And the first warning is as expected`
  40 `And the second warning is as expected`
  41 `And the third warning is as expected`
  42 `Using paired delimiter both fore/aft fails as expected`
  44 `Using extra paired delimiter outside scope fails as expected`
  46 `Reversing delimiters works, as expected within scope of extra delims`
  48 `Using terminating paired delimiter fore, opening aft fails as expected outside scope of extra delims`
  50 `Using nested extra paired delimiters works`
  52 `Using too few closing delims in nesting fails as expected`
(t/op/lex.t lines 314-380; 11 of the file's 41 blessed rows.)

SHAPE: the WORK is PPI's, not PCL's -- PPI 1.291 has no
`extra_paired_delimiters` support, so the tokens do not arrive.  Check what
PPI does with `qÂ«aÂ»` before designing anything here; if PPI mis-lexes it (as
opposed to refusing the document) that is a rule-13 upstream log.  The rows
that assert a FAILURE (42, 44, 48, 52) are principle 9 and belong to
`NS:Error compatibility for invalid Perl input` whatever happens to the
feature; the three warning rows are #221.

So the honest split is: 4 rows NS:invalid-input, 3 rows #221, 4 rows this
task.  Registered as one task because a reader looking at op/lex.t needs one
pointer.

MEASURED (perl 5.40.3): `use utf8; use feature "extra_paired_delimiters"; print q«a«b»c», qq「x」` prints `a«b»c` and `x` -- the opening delimiter closes at its MIRROR and NESTS as a bracket does; `use v5.36; q«a»` is a syntax error ("Unrecognized character \xBB"): the feature is in NO bundle.

PERL'S TABLE (take it from perl's own source, never typed): the perl checkout the companion suite uses, /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/build/perl-5.40.3/perl-5.40.3/unicode_constants.h (generated by regen/unicode_constants.pl): `EXTRA_OPENING_UTF8_BRACKETS` / `EXTRA_CLOSING_UTF8_BRACKETS` (lines 100-101: parallel UTF-8 strings, the Nth opener closes with the Nth closer; ( < [ { first), `EXTRA_OPENING_NON_UTF8_BRACKETS` / `..._CLOSING_...` (lines 104-105: a BYTES source -- no `use utf8` -- has only 0xAB / 0xBB, « and »), `DEPRECATED_OPENING_UTF8_BRACKETS` (line 108: the openers whose use OUTSIDE the feature warns -- op/lex.t's three warning rows, #221).  toke.c `S_scan_str` line 11753 `if (FEATURE_MORE_DELIMS_IS_ENABLED)` chooses the table; the feature bit is FEATURE_MORE_DELIMS_BIT (feature.h line 22).

THE TWO PPI SITES (the branch, a FEATURE group of its own, as AL/AN were for lexical subs / class):
(1) feature state -- PPI::Lexer already tracks features (`$features`, Lexer.pm ~201 / 446 / 648, from PPI::Statement::Include::feature_mods, Include.pm 259) for `try` / `defer` / `class`; the DELIMITER is the Tokenizer's decision, so the Lexer must push "extra_paired_delimiters on/off" to the Tokenizer when it finishes the `use feature` / `no feature` statement (the tokenizer is pulled token by token, so the flag reaches the next token), scoped to the enclosing block the way group AL scopes the names `my sub` declares (a brace-depth stack, emptied by the closing `}`).
(2) the quote-like operator's section start -- Token/_QuoteEngine/Full.pm (the bracket section: `_close` and `_scan_for_brace_character`, ~lines 300-375): with the flag on, an opener found in the table takes its mirror as `_close` and nests; off, the same character stays an ordinary (unpaired) delimiter -- byte-identical tokens for the same text (a twin row).  The table goes into the branch as data generated FROM perl's header (a regen step or a checked-in copy with its source line), with the bytes/utf8 split (a document without `use utf8` sees only « »).
PCL: the quote lowering already takes PPI's `_delimiters` / section offsets; measure `tr«a»«b»`, `s«a»«b»`, `qw«a b»`, `m«a»i` once the tokens arrive.  op/lex.t's 11 rows: 4 assert a FAILURE (42 44 48 52: principle 9, NS invalid input), 3 are #221 (the deprecation warnings), 4 are this feature (37 46 50 + the one-statement form).
